heard: Astronomers built a massive deep space telescope pointed straight down through Earth. Beneath the South Pole, researchers turned a cubic kilometer of ice into the IceCube Observatory. Hot water drills melted holes 2,500 meters deep, freezing 5,000 optical sensors into the ice. Completed in 2010, the array captures neutrinos traveling in straight lines across the cosmos. Atmospheric cosmic rays swamp neutrino signals by roughly one million to one. To block that noise, Ice Cube uses the solid Earth as a physical shield. The detector tracks upward traveling particles from neutrinos that passed entirely through Earth. In September 2017, it pinpointed a neutrino from a blazar 3.7 billion light years away.
